title: Kindness Is a Riot
style: 1981 British art-rock duet, two contrasting male vocals trading lines, a flamboyant operatic tenor with falsetto leaps and scat singing and a cool dry baritone, 112 BPM, A major, dynamic from sparse to enormous, bouncing six-note electric bass riff with a rest, doubled by piano, finger snaps and handclaps, clean chiming guitar arpeggios, bright piano, tight drums, organ pad, multi-tracked choir at the climax, quiet whispered breakdown building to a full-voice peak, ending on bass, snaps and a spoken line, live roomy mix, anxious, compassionate, cathartic
rows: female lead vocals, drum machine, synth-pop, saxophone, trap hi-hats, EDM, rap, autotune

A duet for two contrasting male voices. Voice A is a flamboyant, operatic tenor with a huge range who leaps into falsetto and takes the scat lines, verse lines 1-2 and the climax. Voice B is a cool, dry, slightly detached baritone who takes verse lines 3-4 and speaks the last words. They trade lines, then join in unison on the chorus, with a multi-tracked choir behind them at the climax.
